page: Amazon Web Services c9g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core topology, avoiding the resource contention common in simultaneous multithreading environments. Cache resources comprise 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance lacks bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage options, and includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile without integrated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread efficiency and memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic assessments, the instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core testing (score 2353.0), Geekbench text processing (3161.0), and Passmark memory throughput (score 4296.88). Data manipulation benchmarks display notable performance, with gzip single-threaded compression reaching 36.52 GB/sec and bzip3 single-threaded decompression achieving 17.33 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10 percent. Multi-core performance scales consistently across tasks, recording strong scores in Geekbench multi-core (19897.0), Passmark database operations (29409.23), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (256.09 GB/sec).

From an efficiency standpoint, the dedicated 16-core ARM architecture offers dense per-core compute output without hyperthreading overhead, though compute benchmarks like stress-ng and Passmark CPU remain in the average tier. The configuration lacks local NVMe disks, meaning all operational data persists over the network or in memory. Workloads best aligned with the c9g.4xlarge include compute-bound tasks such as code compilation, static web serving (benchmarked at 54.43 GB/sec), database operations, and lightweight CPU-based language model text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by 16 dedicated AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores running at 3.3 GHz. Configured with a single thread per core, 48 MB of L3 cache, and 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), this instance provides a compute-heavy resource ratio via the Nitro hypervisor. It offers no bundled local storage and features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. In benchmarks, the c9g.4xlarge demonstrates top-tier single-core execution in Geekbench and Passmark memory metrics, as well as high-throughput gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Multi-core capabilities are strong for database operations and static web serving, with average performance across raw stress-ng CPU runs. This makes the instance suitable for distributed batch processing, static web serving, intermediate database engines, and software build pipelines requiring reliable single-thread compute efficiency.
